narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Raibenshe was historically practiced by the Bagdi community in medieval Bengal, who served as bodyguards to regional landlords.
The dance takes its name from the raibansh, a long bamboo stick used in martial displays.
on_screen: Map: India · South Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally linked to the martial duties and bodyguard traditions of the Bagdi community in medieval Bengal, the dance embodies martial prowess and athletic skill.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:A video shows a performance of the martial folk dance Raibenshe at Kolkata during Poush Utsav 2025.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9a/A_video_shows_a_performance_of_the_martial_folk_dance_Raibenshe_at_Kolkata_during_Poush_Utsav_2025.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance features vigorous and manly body movements accompanied by acrobatics using long bamboo sticks.
Male dancers enact martial actions such as drawing a bow, throwing a spear, and waving a sword.
A single brass anklet (nupur) is worn on the right ankle to accent movement.
Watch for Bow Drawing, Spear Throwing, Sword Waving.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Performances are accompanied musically by dhols (traditional double-headed drums) and kanshis (cymbals).
The sound is further accented by the nupur brass anklet on the dancer's right foot.
Listen for the dhol, kanshi, nupur.

A high-energy percussive soundscape created by the beating of dhol drums and the clashing of kanshi brass cymbals, rhythmically punctuated by the metallic jingle of a single brass anklet on the dancer's right foot.

narration: The dance is performed primarily across the Birbhum, Bardhaman, and Murshidabad districts of West Bengal, India.
Originating within the Bagdi community of medieval Bengal, Raibenshe sits within the broader spectrum of Indian folk and Bengali martial dances.
